distinguish between them by noting that effusions appear radiopaque (white) while pneumothorax appears radiolucent (black).", "If the mediastinum is shifted ipsilaterally (towards the opacity), diagnose volume loss causes such as lung collapse, atelectasis, or fibrosis.", "Rule out consolidation (pneumonia) as a primary cause for significant mediastinal shift, as it typically preserves lung volume or causes only minimal shift unless associated with substantial collapse."]}, {"category": "relationship", "trigger": "When evaluating a chest X-ray or CT for suspected congenital lung anomalies, specifically looking for the 'scimitar sign' and associated vascular findings.", "steps": ["Inspect the right hemithorax on the chest X-ray for a curvilinear opacity running parallel to the right heart border (the scimitar vein).", "Assess the position of the mediastinum and trachea;
